title: Masquerade Mind Control Arena
description: The player controls a floating Venice mask that must hunt and capture an animated BrainStem creature in a dark arena. The BrainStem wanders autonomously, and the player must steer the mask to collide with it across multiple rounds of increasing speed. Each successful capture triggers a visual possession effect where the mask latches onto the BrainStem, scores a point, and resets positions for the next round.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a chase-and-capture game. Load BrainStem.glb as an animated creature that wanders the arena autonomously using simple AI (random direction changes every 2 seconds, bouncing off invisible arena walls at radius 12). Play its built-in animation using AnimationMixer. Load venice_mask.glb as the player-controlled hunter, floating at y=1.5 with a gentle bobbing sine motion. The player moves the mask using WASD keys with smooth acceleration and deceleration, max speed starting at 4 units/sec. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 18, 18) looking at origin, with dark ambient light (intensity 0.15) and a SpotLight following the mask to create a searchlight effect. Add a ground plane with a dark grid texture. Implement collision detection between mask and BrainStem using bounding sphere checks (radius 1.5). On collision: (1) play a capture animation where the mask lerps onto the BrainStem and scales down over 1 second, (2) flash the spotlight red, (3) increment score, (4) after 1.5 seconds reset both positions randomly within the arena. The game has 7 rounds. Each round increases BrainStem speed by 15% and decreases the spotlight cone angle by 3 degrees, making hunting harder. Display an HTML overlay showing current round number, score, and a 30-second countdown timer per round. If the timer expires before capture, the round is lost. After all 7 rounds, show a results screen with total captures out of 7. Validate that speed increases each round, spotlight narrows, timer resets, score only increments on valid collision, and positions reset within arena bounds. Add particle burst effects on each capture using BufferGeometry with 50 points that fade out over 1 second. Scale both models appropriately so the mask is roughly head-sized and the BrainStem is slightly larger.
